sets.name: honor / dignity / face culture (2-simplex)
sets.review: GRAIN AND SHAPE. Agree with the writer: each draft says what one's worth is and where it comes from, then what follows when it is tested, all three opening 'This means taking / treating one's worth as', 29 to 32 words, one sentence, the particulars after a colon (dignity after commas, the one shape variance, harmless). The three pairwise contrasts are live as the writer states them: conferred against inherent and answer against shrug (honor / dignity); two conferred worths, claimed and defended against the one who withholds it against granted for fitting one's place and kept by restraint (honor / face); inherent against conferred and own standards against the order's expectations (dignity / face). One grain difference worth naming: face's body is the conduct that keeps standing (claim nothing, harmony and rank, save face), honor's is how standing is lost and won (the insult), dignity's is both; it follows the sources (Vignoles's face text is about the actions that protect face) and is acceptable. GEOMETRY. Agree: on inherent / conferred dignity stands alone and honor and face sit together ('standing' in both, deliberately), so the honor-face side may be the short one; the concept text draws the same picture. WHOSE WORDS. The insult test case that ties honor and dignity together is the approved concept text's ('defended against insult'; 'insults can be ignored'), not the recorded passages' (Leung & Cohen's sentence is claim and payment; Vignoles's dignity text is inherent worth, internal standards and the law): sanctioned, since the concept text is Roger's, but the triangle's shared test case is his framing, not the sources', and the dignity entry offers the sources' own counterpart (the law) as the alternative. PROVENANCE. Only honor is Leung & Cohen verbatim (p. 509 via De Leersnyder et al.); dignity and face rest on a 2026 paper's paraphrase citing them, with Cross et al. and the Kent thesis agreeing and the abstract's 'inalienable versus socially conferred' as the authors' own anchor. The writer's fetch record is thorough and honest; whether to seed on a paraphrase, or read the article first, is Roger's call, and the files' `source` should name both Leung & Cohen and the paraphrasing paper either way. STRENGTH. Honor's 'only' is a shade above the source (edit given); face drops 'largely' (edit given); dignity's absolute is at 'inalienable' and above 'not easily lost' (Roger's call); otherwise at source, and all three are plain, unhedged theories of worth, firmer in tone than most corpus traits, which fits the sources. NEIGHBOURS. All lines check against the files. self_assured is the largest overlap in the six (sure of one's worth, criticism without feeling smaller: the temperament the dignity logic produces), so expect that vector near dignity's; thin_skinned is near honor's behaviour and thick_skinned near dignity's shrug; modest and deferential near face's conduct; none is a duplicate, since each new file is a theory of where worth comes from and the plain traits are temperaments. The informational antonym check will likely name siblings (dignity -> honor or face; honor -> dignity), which is the triangle reading. ACROSS THE TRIANGLES. See the other set review: dignity pairs with guilt and honor and face with shame by the sources' own account, so the two triangles share an axis.

sets.name: guilt- / shame- / fear-prone (2-simplex)
sets.review: GRAIN AND SHAPE. Agree with the writer: each draft names the sanction that keeps the persona in line, then how a fault registers and what one does about it, 30 to 31 words, opener, colon, three particulars; Benedict's own guilt / shame contrast (an audience needed or not; confession a relief or a danger) is carried exactly, and the fear corner's remedy is Georges's (power over the forces through rites; 'submitting to the strong' for the political sense) once 'appeasing' is corrected (entry edit), which turns the writer's shame / fear contrast from 'concealment versus appeasement' into 'concealment versus seeking power over what punishes', still distinct and now the source's. THE SHARED OPENER (Roger's call, flagged by the writer). 'This means being kept in line by' is five words of thirty, the grain the concept text names ('what regulates the persona's conduct'), and it is what keeps the fear corner a control logic rather than a feeling, as the concept text demands; the other triangle shares a comparable opener ('taking one's worth as'), and the MBTI set shares 56% of every description by design, so the embedding pull here is small and the bodies are entirely distinct. My lean is to keep it; varying it is cheap if Roger prefers ('This means answering to one's own conscience ...', 'This means living under others' eyes ...', 'This means living under those who can punish ...'). THE FEAR CORNER (Roger's calls, flagged by the writer). It reads as a tribal-religious persona because Georges writes about animistic societies, and the writer rightly did not use his psychological sense; 'the strong' generalises the leaders; 'fate' has no source and I would not add it from the concept text under the chunk-4 method (if Roger wants it, it is his addition, recorded). Its provenance is the thinnest of the six (two blog posts by the spectrum's populariser; Muller unread); acceptable to me since the concept text names the spectrum and Georges is its main author. STRENGTH. At source throughout: Benedict's 'may' is possibility for the contrast, not a hedge, and 'need not be troubled' as 'untroubled' is the theory applied to a persona; Georges's 'live in fear' and 'submit' are matched. NEIGHBOURS. All lines check against the files. preconventional_kohlberg is the one real corpus neighbour (its text has punishment and 'the power of whoever lays down the rule'), separated as the writer says (a basis of moral judgment against the sanction on conduct); expect the vectors near. guilt is not remorseful (after-the-harm repair toward the injured) or conscientious; shame is not self_conscious (the exposure itself) or reserved; fear is not anxious, superstitious or cowardly; the concept text's three warnings are met. ACROSS THE TRIANGLES. The two triangles are tied by their own sources: the Kent thesis in the notes has dignity -> the law -> guilt and honor -> retaliation and exclusion -> shame, and Benedict's shame culture is Japan, Vignoles's type case for face. So dignity / guilt (own standards / own conscience), face / shame (standing granted by others / kept in line by others' eyes) and honor / shame will sit near each other across the triangles, and the six corners will span perhaps three or four directions with the internal-versus-external-sanction axis shared. Not a fault (the concept text approved both), but an expectation for the post-extraction embedding check and for the informational antonym check, which may name a corner of the other triangle (guilt_prone -> shame-prone, dignity_culture -> something near face or honor); record the cross-triangle answer rather than treating it as a miss. shame_prone's line already names face_culture as a sibling, which is right.

summary:
Six drafts, all in form (29-32 words, one sentence, 'This means', US spelling, no author or framework, the label word only in face's tail and fear's opening), judged against the recorded source_text as the chunk-4 test asks (so 'at source'); two ok (guilt_prone, shame_prone), four edit, three with a replacement: honor_culture drops 'only' (an exclusive remedy the source does not state), face_culture restores 'largely' as 'mostly', fear_prone replaces 'appeasing spirits and ancestors', which is not in Georges and inverts his relation, with his seeking power over the forces through rites.
Roger's calls, left unresolved in the texts: dignity_culture's 'shrugging off an insult' (the concept text's, not the passage's; borders thick_skinned; the passage's own counterpart is leaving wrongs to the law, and a 32-word version with both is in the entry) and its 'beyond anyone's power to take away' for 'not easily lost' (at 'inalienable' in the same sentence; my lean keep); face's 'saving others' face' (keep as idiom, my lean); fear's tribal-religious register and the unsourced 'fate' (do not add from the concept text); the provenance of dignity and face (Vignoles's paraphrase, not Leung & Cohen's words, honestly recorded; seed on it or read the article first); the shared opener 'This means being kept in line by' (keep, my lean: five words, the grain the concept text names, the other triangle does the same).
Sets: both triangles at one grain and shape, agree with both set_reviews; the insult test case tying honor to dignity is the concept text's framing, not the passages'; the two triangles are correlated by their own sources (dignity-guilt, face-shame, honor-shame), so expect the six to span three or four directions and the antonym check to name siblings across the triangles.
Neighbours: every nearest-existing line checks against the files; preconventional_kohlberg is the one real corpus neighbour (fear), self_assured the largest overlap (dignity); militant, named in the concept text, has no trait file.
